options.a: Inside a ventilated attic space well above the ceiling insulation line
options.b: Under a roof overhang next to soffit intake vents
options.c: Open to outdoor air, typically through roof with proper clearance
options.d: Through a sidewall directly below an operable window

distractorExplanations.a: Vents must extend to open outdoor air; ending in an attic, even a ventilated one, releases sewer gas into the building.
distractorExplanations.b: Codes prohibit vent terminals beneath overhangs with soffit vents because sewer gas is drawn back into the attic.
distractorExplanations.d: Vent terminals may not sit directly beneath an openable window; IPC requires 10 ft horizontal or 3 ft above it.

options.a: Flux applied after heating so it does not burn off
options.b: Solder melted by the torch flame onto an unheated, unfluxed joint
options.c: Clean, fluxed fittings heated until solder wicks into joint
options.d: Lead-bearing 50/50 solder for potable water lines

distractorExplanations.b: The fitting must be cleaned, fluxed, and heated so solder melts on the metal and wicks in; flame-melted solder on cold metal will not bond.
distractorExplanations.a: Flux goes on cleaned surfaces before heating; applying it after heating defeats its cleaning and wetting role.
distractorExplanations.d: Since 1986, solder for potable lines must be lead-free (0.2% lead max); 50/50 tin-lead is prohibited there.
